NJ-2026-S3546.title: Permits mortgage loan originators to work from remote locations under certain circumstances.

actions.text: Received in the Assembly, Referred to Assembly Housing Committee
Passed by the Senate (39-0)
Reported from Senate Committee, 2nd Reading
Introduced in the Senate, Referred to Senate Commerce Committee

NJ-2026-S3546.aiSummary: The bill would let mortgage loan originators and certain licensed workers do their job from home or another remote place if they follow written rules for supervision and security. It would apply only when company systems and customer data are handled under a written security plan, no in-person customer meetings happen at a home unless it is a licensed site, and paper records are not kept at the remote site. The Senate passed it, and it then went to the Assembly.

NJ-2026-A5736.title: Requires school districts to provide 30-minute lunch period for students.

actions.text: Introduced, Referred to Assembly Education Committee

NJ-2026-A5736.aiSummary: The bill would require school districts to give students on full school days a lunch period of at least 30 minutes. It would also bar districts from making any student go more than five hours of class time without lunch, and it would not allow lunch to be combined with the required recess period. The rule would not apply to students in half-day programs and would take effect immediately.

NJ-2026-A5731.title: Establishes two-year pilot program to recognize certain noncredit programs in county college operational aid; appropriates $5 million.

actions.text: Introduced, Referred to Assembly Higher Education Committee

NJ-2026-A5731.aiSummary: The bill would create a two-year pilot program to give county colleges extra state aid for certain noncredit job training programs. These programs would be for short-term workforce needs and may lead to a credential, certification, or license in a high-demand field. It would provide $5 million each year of the pilot from the Workforce Development Partnership Fund.

NJ-2026-A5727.title: Directs BPU to authorize construction and operation of micro-reactors.

actions.text: Introduced, Referred to Assembly Telecommunications and Utilities Committee

NJ-2026-A5727.aiSummary: The bill would require the New Jersey Board of Public Utilities to let micro-reactors be built and run in the state. Micro-reactors are advanced nuclear reactors that make 20 megawatts or less of power. The reactor design would need approval from the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission, and the act would take effect right away.

NJ-2026-A5722.title: Requires hotels and harm reduction service providers to cooperate in providing opioid antidotes and harm reduction supplies at hotels.

actions.text: Introduced, Referred to Assembly Tourism, Gaming and the Arts Committee

NJ-2026-A5722.aiSummary: The bill would require hotels and harm reduction service providers to work together to provide opioid antidotes, such as naloxone, and harm reduction supplies at hotels. It would let hotels connect with registered harm reduction groups to hand out these supplies and train hotel staff on how to use opioid antidotes. The Health Department would also have to help link harm reduction services with hotels and hotel staff.

NJ-2026-A5718.title: Requires Commissioner of Education to appoint independent investigators for complaints against DOE regarding special education.

actions.text: Introduced, Referred to Assembly Education Committee

NJ-2026-A5718.aiSummary: The bill would require the Education Commissioner to appoint an outside, neutral investigator for complaints about special education services against the state Education Department or its offices. The investigator would need to review the complaint, let the person who filed it add more information, and let the department respond. A written decision would be due within 60 days and would be final. The law would take effect on the first day of the second month after it is signed.

NJ-2026-A5713.title: Permits establishment of hookah lounges under certain conditions; establishes municipal application deadlines.

actions.text: Introduced, Referred to Assembly Oversight, Reform and Federal Relations Committee

NJ-2026-A5713.aiSummary: The bill would let hookah lounges operate under set rules in New Jersey if they register with the local health board and meet smoking-area and ventilation requirements. A lounge would have to keep people under 21 out of the smoking area, and it could not allow cannabis or illegal drugs. Municipalities would have to check whether an application is complete within 10 business days and approve or deny a complete application within 30 calendar days.

NJ-2026-A4796.title: Expands criminal and civil penalties for human trafficking, and expands human trafficking training requirements for law enforcement.*

actions.text: Substituted by S3946 (3R)
Reported out of Assembly Comm. with Amendments, 2nd Reading
Transferred to Assembly Judiciary Committee
Reported out of Asm. Comm. with Amendments, and Referred to Assembly Appropriations Committee
Introduced, Referred to Assembly Public Safety and Preparedness Committee

NJ-2026-A4796.aiSummary: Would expand criminal and civil penalties for human trafficking. It would also add more human trafficking training requirements for law enforcement. The changes would affect people accused of trafficking and police officers.

NJ-2026-A2054.title: Requires Division of Children's System of Care to make changes to certain polices regarding the provision of family support and respite care services for certain eligible individuals.

actions.text: Passed by the Assembly (79-0-0)
Reported out of Assembly Committee, 2nd Reading
Reported and Referred to Assembly Appropriations Committee
Reported and Referred to Assembly Aging and Human Services Committee
Introduced, Referred to Assembly Children, Families and Food Security Committee

NJ-2026-A2054.aiSummary: The bill would require the Division of Children’s System of Care to change its rules for family support and respite care for some people under 21 with developmental disabilities. It would set a 12-month approval period, give families a separate bank of respite hours, and require an annual review, while also letting families stay with the same agency after the review. The act would take effect immediately and has passed the Assembly.

NJ-2026-A1406.title: Requires AG to review Statewide policy regarding investigation of human trafficking.

actions.text: Passed by the Assembly (79-0-0)
Reported out of Assembly Committee, 2nd Reading
Introduced, Referred to Assembly Judiciary Committee

NJ-2026-A1406.aiSummary: The Attorney General would have to review and update the state policy for investigating human trafficking, if needed. The review would look at whether undercover police should use audio or video recordings, how to control sharing those recordings, and how county prosecutors should be involved from the start of local investigations. It would affect state, county, and town law enforcement and people who are victims of human trafficking.
